main_text.p: optimè libro primo de legibus sub personâ Megilli Lacedæmonii: Quod omnes homines summopere in voluptates vehementissimas, atque in petulantiam & insaniam trahit, id ab universâ regione lex nostra exterminavit: nec in agris, nec in urbibus quas Spartani habent, compotationes cernas, sed nec compotationibus conjunctas, quibus ad omnem voluptatem movemur. Nec ullus est, qui alicui ebrietate lascivienti obvium factus non maximâ eum poenâ statim afficiat, ita ut nec Bacchanalium tempus ad impunitatem prodesse ebrio queat. Hactenus ille. Quam fœdam turpitudinem ut profligarent à republicâ suâ Lacones,[illegible, ~2 letters] nebriabant servos suos, & ebrios ineptientesque in convivia introductos iunioribus ostendebant, ut averfari & [?]diffe pestem hanc corporum & animorum, ut loquitur Xenophon, & pofl[illegible, ~1 letter][illegible, ~2 letters]m Plato, discerent, ac ultra sitim non sibere consuescerent. In cæteris Græciæ urbibus, inquit Xenophon, mali cum bonis eodem foro utuntur, cum iis sæpe sedent, sæpe ludunt, si velint, & sa[illegible, ~2 letters]is habetur, si mali tantummodo dicantur. page.notes: Left margin: only cut-off fragments of marginal notes remain at the scan edge; they cannot be read and are marked as illegible at their approximate positions. Right margin empty. Line 2 of the paragraph reads "sibere" for the printed word at the line start, which is partly hidden. Several line-start letters are cut off by the scan edge: "[?]diffe" (probably "odiffe", i.e. odisse), "[?]iro" (probably "viro"), and "[?]m Plato" (the word before "Plato" is not legible). Long s is transcribed as s throughout. Words with probable long-s printing (ditcerent, fitim, confuefcerent, fi) are normalised to s. Bottom of page: show-through from the reverse side ("rem mi...") is excluded. The catchword at bottom right is doubtful.
